comparison: Perfect agreement on demographic data (C12-C18). Both evaluations find the cohort composition well-defined and appropriate. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the sample size and inclusion of fertile controls as strengths.
Complete agreement on baseline reproductive parameters (C19-C26). Both find the characterization of study groups convincing and well-supported by statistical evidence in Table 1.

Full concordance on clustering analysis (C27-C32, C58-C60, C65). Both evaluations accept the three-cluster finding as methodologically sound. Peer reviewers noted alignment with previous observations.
Complete agreement on network analysis (C35-C40). Both find the SparCC-based co-occurrence patterns appropriate and complementary to clustering analysis. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Full agreement on negative findings (C41-C43, C61, C63, C66, C138). Both evaluations accept that global microbiota features do not differentiate fertility status, recognizing this as an important finding rather than a limitation.

Strong concordance on Flavobacterium associations (C55-C57, C62, C67, C100-C101). Both evaluations highlight this as the most robust finding. Peer reviewers explicitly named Flavobacterium as a key result that survived multiple testing correction.

Complete agreement on future directions (C140-C143). Both evaluations support the appropriateness of proposed follow-up studies. Peer reviewers noted clinical relevance for researchers working on microbiome and male fertility.

Strong agreement on contamination controls (C71-C74, C153-C154). Both evaluations praise the inclusion of negative controls and decontamination methods. Peer reviewers explicitly highlighted this as a methodological strength. OpenEval also addresses clustering methodology (C75) not specifically mentioned by peer reviewers.

Agreement on study limitations (C126-C128, C131-C133). Both evaluations accept the acknowledged limitations as appropriate. Peer reviewers noted authors addressed concerns from previous review rounds. OpenEval also discusses 16S limitations (C129-C130) not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewers.

Partial overlap on bacterial associations. OpenEval rates C46-C54 as UNCERTAIN due to lack of FDR correction, while peer reviewers accept 'specific associations' as part of well-conducted study. Peer review also includes C119-C120, C124, C137, C139 which OpenEval evaluates separately with UNCERTAIN ratings.

Agreement on species-level findings (C33-C34). Both accept the lack of species-level clustering. Peer review also includes C81 (bacterial origins) which OpenEval evaluates separately in R15. Both find the transient colonization interpretation reasonable.

Partial agreement on comparison to prior literature. Both address C76-C78 regarding alignment with previous studies. Peer review also covers sample size (C64) and methodological critiques (C68-C70) which OpenEval evaluates in separate results (R26, R17).

Both address clustering methodology (C75). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of silhouette score approach (C75, C155-C156), while peer reviewers implicitly accept this through praise of contamination controls and overall methodology.

Divergent assessment. OpenEval rates Lactobacillus associations (C119-C120, C137) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of FDR correction, while peer reviewers accept these as part of 'specific associations' in a well-conducted study.
Divergent assessment. OpenEval rates Prevotella associations (C124-C125) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of FDR correction, while peer reviewers accept these findings within the overall positive evaluation.

Both address C139 (nuanced conclusion about specific taxa vs. global features). OpenEval finds this appropriately cautious, while peer reviewers accept it as part of the study's 'potential connection' between microbiome and fertility.
